research_rationale: Identity and text: the order was read in full in the registered Federal Register original (6 FR 1517, issue of 1941-03-20, PDF page 1; grade original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original true). Number 8714 is printed in the bracket after the signature, signed March 18, 1941, title 'Designating Certain Officers To Act as Secretary of the Treasury in Case of Absence or Sickness of the Secretary', agreeing with the census register row. Inventory: one sole paragraph with three succession designations (Fiscal Assistant Secretary; senior Assistant Secretary on duty; General Counsel) and a revocation of Executive Order No. 6202-B. End: Executive Order 10586, signed January 13, 1955 (20 FR 361, issue of 1955-01-15, held), orders that EO 8714 of March 18, 1941 "is hereby revoked", naming it by number, date and title. The dossier also lists EO 10588 as a revoking order; that record comes from the same Federal Register page extract, which prints EOs 10586, 10587 and 10588 one after another, and EO 10588 (President's Commission on Veterans' Pensions) does not mention EO 8714, so it is neither an end nor a later event. Held evidence only; the order is a NO.
savings_reason: EO 10586 independently designates the Under Secretary for Monetary Affairs, the Assistant Secretaries in the order the Secretary fixes, and the General Counsel to act as Secretary of the Treasury, so the function the order served continues under a separate command. The revocation of Executive Order No. 6202-B contained in EO 8714 was accomplished when EO 8714 took effect; EO 10586 contains no wording reviving it. EO 10586 has no savings clause for EO 8714.
earlier_end_check: Own terms: each designation operates "until such absence or sickness shall cease", which bounds each period of service, not the standing designation, which applies again at every later absence; it supplies no end. The dossier chain lists only EO 10586 and the unrelated EO 10588 page neighbour; the reverse-citation search in LOOKUPS.md finds no other held text that names EO 8714 with a change verb. No held source shows repeal before 1955-01-13 of the statutory authority (Revised Statutes sections 177 and 179); EO 10586 itself cites section 179. Search coverage: the later-events catalogue (OFR disposition notes from 1937) and the held order texts; Public Land Orders and Civil Service Commission notices printed in issues without an executive order are not searched.
scope_check: One clause. EO 10586 revokes the whole order by number, date and title; no partial reading is indicated, and no amendment of EO 8714 is held.
independent_command_check: The revocation of EO 6202-B inside the order was performed at issue and is a spent command whose consequence is not undone by the later revocation of EO 8714. EO 10586's own designations are a separate command.
savings_check: No savings, exception or nothing-herein wording in EO 10586 as read; accrued effects of acts done under EO 8714 are not disturbed by a prospective revocation.

research_rationale: Identity and text: read in full in the registered Federal Register original (6 FR 5708, issue of 1941-11-11, PDF page 2; grade original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original true). Order 8937 of November 7, 1941, 'Extending the Period of Eligibility on Civil Service Registers or Lists of Persons Who Serve in the Armed Forces of the United States', provides that service after May 1, 1940 is not counted in determining eligibility period, with a proviso on notice to the Commission, and supersedes Executive Order No. 8602. Inventory: one sole paragraph. Later event: EO 9579 (signed June 30, 1945, held APP transcription, page check done) restates the proviso, effective as of December 8, 1944. End: EO 9830, Part III (official Federal Register text, 12 FR 1259, held with its PDF) revokes the listed orders including "No. 8937 of November 7, 1941." The dossier had no ACT record for this pair; the naming is supplied as the held excerpt SUPPLEMENT:FR9830P3 and the enacting clause as SUPPLEMENT:FR9830ENACT.
savings_reason: EO 9830 Rule II section 2.1(b) independently provides that "the names of persons who lost eligibility on a probational register because of service in the armed forces subsequent to May 1, 1940" may be entered on registers, an independent command covering the persons EO 8937 protected. EO 9830 has no savings wording for revoked orders.
earlier_end_check: Own terms: the forty-day notice proviso is an applicant deadline (later ninety days), not an end of the order; May 1, 1940 is a coverage start date. EO 9579 is an amendment, a later event, not an end. Held texts that mention EO 8937 are EO 9579, EO 9580 and an index entry on the same page (recitals or amendment) and EO 9830; none revokes it.
